world-scholars-cup-tashkent-round-2027.about:
The World Scholar's Cup (WSC) is an international academic tournament for school students that rewards curiosity rather than memorisation. Teams of three study an interdisciplinary annual theme spanning science, history, art, music, literature and social studies, then compete in four events: Team Debate, Collaborative Writing, the Scholar's Challenge (an individual multiple-choice test) and the Scholar's Bowl (a team quiz). Rounds also include community events such as the Scholar's Show (talent show).

This is a regional round in Tashkent, Uzbekistan, on 22–24 March 2027, hosted by British School of Tashkent. Students can join through a school club or as an independent team of three from any country; results can qualify teams for a Global Round and, from there, the Tournament of Champions at Yale University.
highlights: Four team events: debate, collaborative writing, quiz bowl and challenge test
Open to independent teams as well as school clubs
Qualifies strong teams for a Global Round and the Yale Tournament of Champions
world-scholars-cup-tashkent-round-2027.eligibility: School students (typically ages 10–18) in teams of three, from any school or country; independent teams are welcome. Divisions: Senior (born on or before 1 July 2013) and Junior (younger); scholars must be born on or before 31 December 2014.
how_to_apply: Form a team of three (school club or independent)
Open the WSC registration portal and choose this round (or use the round's Request Info link)
Register the team and any accompanying adults, and pay the fee by card or bank transfer
Study the 2026–27 theme and curriculum before the round
Attend the round in Tashkent, 22–24 March 2027
world-scholars-cup-tashkent-round-2027.costs: Registration fee per scholar (student): regular 750000 UZS, late 1000000 UZS. Adults/coaches register separately; travel, accommodation and most meals are extra. Payment by card or bank transfer through the WSC portal.

world-scholars-cup-tokyo-yokohama-mini-g.about:
Global Rounds are the second stage of the World Scholar's Cup: teams that qualified at a regional round meet scholars from many countries for several days of Team Debate, Collaborative Writing, the Scholar's Challenge and the Scholar's Bowl, plus the Scholar's Show, cultural fair and Scholar's Ball. The Tokyo-Yokohama Mini Global Round runs 11–15 December 2026 with Pacifico Yokohama as the main venue; debates are held at nearby schools.

Teams register with the round's registration form linked on the event page. The ground partner JTB offers official hotel packages for six nights (10–16 December) within walking distance of the venue, and optional tours. Strong results qualify teams for the Tournament of Champions at Yale University.
highlights: Global Round stage of the World Scholar's Cup in Japan
All four team events plus Scholar's Show and Ball
Qualifies teams for the Tournament of Champions at Yale
world-scholars-cup-tokyo-yokohama-mini-g.eligibility: School students who qualified at a World Scholar's Cup regional round, in teams of three; see the Global Round page for capacity and qualification details.
how_to_apply: Check that your team qualified at a regional round
Download and complete the registration form on the round page
Book an official hotel package through JTB if needed
Prepare the 2026–27 theme
Attend the round in Yokohama, 11–15 December 2026
world-scholars-cup-tokyo-yokohama-mini-g.costs: Registration fee per scholar set in the registration form; JTB hotel packages (6 nights, breakfast included) from about JPY 107,000 per guest in triple occupancy; flights and visas extra.

world-scholars-cup-tournament-of-champio.about:
The Tournament of Champions is the final of the World Scholar's Cup season, hosted with the Yale International Relations Association at Yale University, New Haven, on 12–18 November 2026. Scholars compete again in Team Debate, Collaborative Writing, the Scholar's Challenge and the Scholar's Bowl, and also attend a panel on college life and admissions, talks by keynote speakers including a Yale professor, the Yale Ball and a scavenger hunt.

Only qualified teams can attend: all three scholars must have qualified at a 2026 Global Round (or the 2025 Dubai Holiday Special Global Round), with at least two who qualified as teammates, and all participants must be at least 11 years old. Delegation coordinators register qualified teams through the WSC ToC registration portal; visa invitation letters are available on request.
highlights: Season final of the World Scholar's Cup at Yale University
Panel on college life and admissions, Yale Ball and keynote speakers
Scholars from over fifty countries
world-scholars-cup-tournament-of-champio.eligibility: Only scholars who qualified at a 2026 Global Round (or the 2025 Dubai Holiday Special Global Round); at least two teammates must have qualified together; minimum age 11.
how_to_apply: Confirm your team's qualification from a 2026 Global Round
Sign in to the ToC registration portal with the coordinator email used at the Global Round
Register the team and adults, and request a visa invitation letter if needed
Book official hotels/shuttles via the Tournament of Champions page
Attend the tournament at Yale, 12–18 November 2026
world-scholars-cup-tournament-of-champio.costs: Registration fee per scholar shown in the ToC portal; shuttle from official hotels USD 140 for the event; flights, hotels and visas extra. Refund rules depend on cancellation date (see FAQ on the event page).
